siblings.summary: Seven places to sleep within a 20-minute walk of Cartmel's Michelin three-star dining room.

siblings.summary: Eleven characterful places to sleep near L'Enclume, ranked by taxi minutes back to Cartmel.

siblings.summary: What to do around Cartmel within a 30 km radius, graded by half-day, full-day and after-dinner picks.

sources.title: L'Enclume — Stay
sources.claim: L'Enclume's room rate Tue-Sat bundles the dinner reservation and breakfast at Rogan & Co.

sources.title: L'Enclume — Our Rooms
sources.claim: Sixteen individually designed rooms in four categories, scattered across village cottages and a townhouse.

sources.title: Stray Sleep Eat — L'Enclume Cartmel
sources.claim: The advertised DB&B Package is Tue-Fri only — a Saturday booking is room + dinner billed separately.

sources.title: Cool Places — Cavendish Arms
sources.claim: Cavendish Arms £75–£125 with breakfast on the same street as the restaurant.

sources.title: The Kings Arms Cartmel
sources.claim: Six rooms named after Romantic poets in a 300-year-old building overlooking the Square and Priory.

sources.title: The Royal Oak — Rooms
sources.claim: Refurbished en-suite king rooms over the pub on the Square; breakfast included.

sources.title: Cartmel Old Grammar
sources.claim: Twelve rooms in a Georgian boutique country house, six minutes from the Square.

sources.title: Aynsome Manor
sources.claim: 5-star Georgian manor B&B in open meadowland; locally-sourced Cartmel breakfast and complimentary chauffeur service for the local area.

sources.title: Linthwaite House (Leeu Collection)
sources.claim: Hilltop country house above Windermere with Simon Rogan's Henrock restaurant on-site; private tarn with row boats.

sources.title: Rome2Rio — Bowness to Cartmel
sources.claim: Cartmel ↔ Bowness is a 20-minute, €30–45 taxi.

sources.title: Holker Hall — Gardens
sources.claim: HHA Garden of the Year 1991; 400-year-old Great Lime ('50 Great British Tree'); Cascade with Neptune statue.

sources.title: Lakeside & Haverthwaite Railway — Fares
sources.claim: Tickets sold on the day at the station only — no online or advance booking.

sources.title: Blackwell Arts & Crafts House
sources.claim: Mackay Hugh Baillie Scott's 1898–1900 Grade I-listed Arts & Crafts masterpiece overlooking Bowness; closed Sundays.

sources.title: Windermere Lake Cruises — Freedom of the Lake
sources.claim: Freedom of the Lake £32 adult unlocks the full Bowness–Lakeside–Ambleside triangle for 24 hours.

sources.title: Walk Lakes — Hampsfell Hospice
sources.claim: Hampsfell Hospice 5.6 km / 225 m / 1h 25 — single highest-payoff short outing in the radius.

sources.title: The Hazelmere
sources.claim: 1897 Grange-over-Sands tearoom; over 100 leaf teas; award-winning afternoon tea with Lyth Valley damson preserve.

sources.title: Cartmel Racecourse — 2026 dates
sources.claim: Bank Holiday triple Sat 23 / Mon 25 / Wed 27 May 2026 makes the village busy and parking impossible.

sources.title: IET Lancashire & Cumbria — Events
sources.claim: 'Wings Over Windermere' evening talk at The Netherwood Hotel & Spa in Grange-over-Sands on Thu 3 Dec 2026.

sources.title: BMVC 2026
sources.claim: British Machine Vision Conference at Lancaster Town Hall, 23–26 Nov 2026.

sources.title: EAI SecureComm 2026
sources.claim: 22nd International Conference on Security & Privacy in Communication Networks at Lancaster University, 21–24 Jul 2026.

sources.title: Cartmel Priory
sources.claim: 1190 Augustinian foundation; medieval jewel; 26 carved choir misericords.

sources.title: Cartmel Priory — Visit
sources.claim: Free entry, 10:00–16:00 Monday–Saturday; closed Sundays for services.

sources.title: Cartmel Village Shop
sources.claim: Original home of sticky toffee pudding — over 30 years of baking; Rick Stein 'Food Hero'.

sources.title: Unsworth's Yard
sources.claim: Courtyard off Ford Road with a five-barrel brewery, Cartmel Cheeses, Oscar's wine bar and a pizzeria.

sources.title: Brantwood — Visit
sources.claim: John Ruskin's home on the east shore of Coniston Water; £16.50 adult; house 10:30–16:00.

sources.title: National Trust — Hill Top
sources.claim: Beatrix Potter's farmhouse — timed-ticket pre-book mandatory, even for NT members.

sources.title: Tarn Hows circular walk
sources.claim: 2-mile firm gravel loop, wheelchair/pushchair friendly; free Tramper mobility scooters bookable 48 hr ahead.

sources.title: Steam Yacht Gondola
sources.claim: Restored 1859 Victorian steamer; operates Tue/Wed/Thu/Sat; book up to 4 weeks ahead.

sources.title: Sizergh Castle (NT)
sources.claim: 14th-century pele tower, Strickland family seat since 1239; NT's largest limestone rock garden.

sources.title: Levens Hall
sources.claim: World's oldest topiary garden — Guillaume Beaumont, 1694, trained under Le Notre at Versailles.

sources.title: Lakeland Motor Museum
sources.claim: ~30,000 exhibits at Backbarrow with the Campbell Bluebird Exhibition for the 21 world land and water speed records.

sources.title: Brockhole — Lake District Visitor Centre
sources.claim: Treetop Trek and Treetop Nets high ropes, kayak and SUP hire, 30-acre adventure playground.

sources.title: RSPB Leighton Moss
sources.claim: North-west England's largest reedbed: bitterns, marsh harriers, bearded tits; 9 m Skytower.

sources.title: The Cavendish Arms
sources.claim: 500-year-old Grade II listed coaching inn on Cavendish Street, a stone's throw from L'Enclume.

sources.title: Michelin Guide — Heft
sources.claim: Michelin-starred 17th-century inn in High Newton with five rooms; Kevin Tickle, eight years at L'Enclume.

sources.title: Windermere Lake Cruises — Cruises
sources.claim: Four colour-coded routes from a 1,300-passenger fleet; MV Tern (1891), Teal (1936), Swan (1938).

sources.title: Guide Over Sands — The Guides
sources.claim: Michael Wilson, current King's Guide to the Sands — royally-appointed Morecambe Bay crossing guide.

sources.title: Walk Lakes — Gummer's How
sources.claim: Gummer's How 2.3 km / 118 m / 40 min — highest reward-per-step walk in the radius, views over Windermere.

sources.title: Coniston Launch
sources.claim: Year-round diesel-electric service across Coniston Water; 15% online discount; hop-on/hop-off Yellow route.

sources.title: Holker Hall
sources.claim: Cavendish family seat, 3 km from L'Enclume; gardens, hall and estate.
